prompts.title: Current model: rear panel repair only
prompts.text:
Modify the existing Cathexis_Body_v1 model. This is a LOCAL REAR SKIRT REPAIR, not a new character generation. Use the attached rear-panel reference to understand the missing cloth, and the existing 3D model as the authority for everything else.

Add ONLY the missing central rear fabric between the existing left and right skirt panels, hanging from beneath the rear waist drape to the lower ankles, just above the heels. Join/overlap it naturally beneath the existing panel edges so the rear skirt is continuous. The material must match the existing worn gray-ivory cloth.

The new cloth hangs BEHIND the legs with physical clearance. Neither knee nor shin may punch through it. Do not make knee-shaped holes, two separate leg coverings or a narrow strip between exposed legs. Keep the actual legs and joints intact behind the fabric. Preserve the front opening; do not fill it or bridge fabric through the body. Preserve both heels and their visibility below the hem.

Leave every other part unchanged: existing side panels, their folds and hem lengths, outer skirt width and silhouette, crown size/design, head, face, hair, reactor, torso, arms, hands, hip canisters, legs and heels. Do not enlarge the crown or regenerate the costume. Do not use the discarded full-dress redesigns. Do not change masks or the face seat in this repair task.

Work on a copy. Preserve the original master and delivery model. If your tools cannot add this local section while preserving the rest, report that limitation and stop; do not substitute whole-body regeneration. We can finish the local mesh repair offline.

Deliver Cathexis_Body_v1_RearPanelFix as a textured unrigged GLB and FBX, with the repaired section separately named where supported. Keep the original scale, pose and materials. Preserve existing UVs outside the added section if the tool supports a local edit; disclose any topology, UV or texture changes. Report actual triangle counts. Provide rear, rear three-quarter and side inspection views showing continuous fabric and knee clearance. Do not start rigging or a new animation bank yet.

The reference illustrates the repair intent. It does not establish mesh topology or animation clearance; those will be checked in the production viewer before replacing the current body.

prompts.title: Body
prompts.text:
For repair of the existing v1 body, use 08-rear-panel-repair.txt instead. The instructions below are for a full rebuild only.

Create CATHEXIS for Loopforge from the THREE attached body reference images: 01-cathexis-body-front.260b685edbc8b769.jpg, 02-cathexis-rear-panel-repair.5385077857a25085.jpg and 03-cathexis-body-left.7876f6e8730e1f86.jpg.

This task is the BODY ONLY. Do not install a porcelain face mask. Separate masks will follow as separate assets. Do not infer additional characters from any reference sheet.

Identity: a theatrical robot diva who runs the Burn-in Theatre. Cracked ivory armor, black articulated mechanics, antique brass corset ribs, compact diadem/headset, amber eye emitters and hip canisters, a compact back reactor, grouped cable-hair and a distressed open-front layered skirt. Elegant, commanding and unmistakably mechanical. Preserve the approved body proportions and high-heeled mechanical feet. Do not turn her into a worker, a glossy generic android, a princess or a weapon-bearing fighter.

The faceplate and mechanical expression insert are separate replaceable items. Keep the permanent compact skull, crown, hair, amber eye emitters and a shallow oval receiving seat. The mechanical face pictured in the body reference is an assembly placeholder: do NOT fuse its teeth, lips, brows or grin into the immutable skull. If object separation is supported, deliver it as a separately named placeholder; otherwise explain the limitation and preserve the neutral master for offline separation before the rig/motion bank. We will not stack a second face over fused facial geometry. No facial rig is claimed at this stage.

She is physically delicate and made for performance and fine interaction, not coarse industrial labor. Keep fine hands, porcelain and elegant costume. Later oil/soot and brewery-residue appearances will reuse this EXACT model, UVs and rig. Do not create a heavier dirty-body replacement. Anger and distress will be expressed through fitted face variants and acting, independent of dirt or mask coverage.

Generate the complete unrigged visual master first, in a clean symmetric A-pose. Hands clear of the torso, five separate mechanical fingers with a distinct thumb, legs and feet separated. The front view is the authority for proportions. Use the rear for reactor/hair construction and the profile for depth. Resolve minor view disagreements coherently rather than duplicating parts.

Keep fabric clear of legs and hands. The skirt has the original layered side panels and an open front. Its central rear cloth must form a continuous section behind the legs, reaching the lower ankles without knee/shin intersections. Use the revised rear reference for this section only; preserve the original outer silhouette, side hems and crown. The original profile predates this rear infill and must not reintroduce the missing rear section. Hair is grouped into a few controllable locks/cable bundles, not thousands of separate strands. Do not bake background shadows, ambient glow, fog, transparent veils or magical energy into geometry. Surface cracks, weave and fine wear should primarily be texture detail.

Where your tools support it, keep body, skirt panels and hair sections separable. Do not claim separate objects unless the exported file actually contains them. If segmentation is unsupported, say so and preserve the neutral master for our offline cleanup. Do not discard the costume just to make auto-rigging easier.

Deliver:
- Cathexis_Body_v1_master: full-detail unrigged source.
- Cathexis_Body_v1_50k: a derivative around 40,000–55,000 triangles, preserving silhouette, fingers, face seating rim and costume. Report the actual count rather than claiming the target was exact.
- Textured GLB and FBX, neutral A-pose, PBR base color, normal, roughness and metallic maps. 2K working textures are sufficient for the first trial; preserve higher-resolution source maps if available.
- A brief report of material slots, separate objects, pose and any likely rigging problems.

Stop before generating the large animation bank. We will inspect the body, fit a mask and test the rig first. Do not overwrite the master when remeshing.

prompts.title: Face system
prompts.text:
CATHEXIS — one permanent head, replaceable mechanism, porcelain coverage
Generate separate items one at a time; never upload the whole face gallery as one object.

1. Fit master: use 04-mask-grace as the porcelain identity reference. Generate a hollow rigid faceplate with a consistent thin oval seating rim, readable expression, eye apertures and attachment features. No eyes, skull, hair, crown or neck. Fit it to the accepted body before expanding the bank. The body owns the amber eyes.
2. Exposed mechanical expression insert: use 10-mechanism-grimace as ONE standalone object. Dark metal/brass brow, cheek and jaw plates, connected backing, open eye apertures and no duplicate skull. Use 11-mechanism-fury and 12-mechanism-distress for two separate expression variants with the same mounting boundary. Fury must shout/snarl, distress must be downturned; do not make every mechanical face happy. For the first prototype these are rigid swaps, not a promised facial rig. A composed neutral mechanism can be derived offline from the accepted insert if needed; no separate neutral image is supplied.
3. Full porcelain family: Grace, Rapture, Scorn, Grief, Fury, Distress. Keep each as a separate rigid asset; expression is not a new body or new head. Do not assume generated contours match perfectly: normalize to the fitted master offline.
4. Split coverage: use 13-mask-half-shell as the separate retained half-shell. 14-split-assembly-reference only shows the desired combination with the mechanical insert; do not generate a fused complete head from it. Mirror the visual side only if explicitly chosen; preserve the chosen orientation in filenames.

The same head can show full porcelain, half porcelain / exposed mechanism, or exposed mechanism alone. The expression underneath must suit the visible emotion. Avoid overlapping teeth, doubled lips or two complete noses. Validate mouth cavities and clearance with ALL fitted combinations; some incompatible pairs may need variant-specific clearance or hidden underlying regions.

Keep a high-resolution master and economical close-review derivatives. Porcelain target around 1–3k triangles each, mechanism around 3–6k as an initial proposal; preserve silhouette before count. Export separate named textured GLBs/FBXs, report actual object/material counts, axes and dimensions. A static image does not establish matching geometry, fitting tolerances, topology or articulation.

Small jaw/brow motion can be added after the rigid expression prototypes pass. No rubber face, live fracture simulation, floating shards, eyes baked into each mask or new full head per expression. Exact face fit, hand-to-mask contacts and swaps belong to offline assembly and actual viewer review.

prompts.title: Rig tests
prompts.text:
CATHEXIS — first rig and motion tests

Use the approved Cathexis_Body_v1 derivative. Keep the unrigged visual master. Do not regenerate her body, costume, materials or proportions for each animation.

Create a Mixamo-compatible humanoid rig in a clean neutral A-pose. Crown and mechanical underface should follow the head rigidly; torso reactor follows the torso and hip canisters follow the pelvis. Face masks are separate rigid attachments and should not be fused into the skin or auto-rigged as anatomy.

Important: skirt and hair must not weld the legs together or become uncontrolled rubber. If your rigging tool cannot separate or sensibly weight these parts, report the limitation and provide the neutral export for offline cleanup. Do not replace the distinctive costume with generic clothing. We can add dedicated skirt/hair bones and rigid plate weighting offline.

Hands need five separate fingers for later mask handling. Report the ACTUAL exported finger bones and weighting. If only hand/wrist bones exist, say that explicitly. Broad gesture tests can proceed, but exact mask handling will remain an offline task.

First apply ONLY these four tests:
1. Hot Walk — our ONLY approved locomotion gait; the prior exported source is Confident_Walk, catalog Action 106. Use that exact source as the first comparison. Keep Hot Walk as our label and retain the source ID/name. If your UI label differs, report the mapping.
2. Mirror_Viewing — Action 48. Test hand/head/face and hair clearance; not yet a finished mask-change animation.
3. Happy_Sway_Standing — Action 415. Test relaxed presence, weight shifts, skirt and heel clearance. Do not assume the source is already a seamless idle loop.
4. Head_Hold_in_Pain — Action 391. Audition head-holding frustration from the conveyor art; test crown, hair and hand clearance. A pain source label does not impose an injury state.

A diagnostic rest pose is required. She NEVER runs and has NO alert state. Do not request ordinary walk/run/alert clips. If the tool automatically bundles them, label them excluded and report that; they must not enter the game bank. No regular worker walk or generic breathing idle as a silent fallback.

Export each test as a textured GLB with the RIGGED CHARACTER INCLUDED, plus FBX. Keep a separate neutral rigged GLB/FBX. Use the Mixamo skeleton template consistently. If exporting all added animations as one file is supported, also supply it, but keep individual exports so missing clips can be checked.

Use clear aliases:
Cathexis_Body_v1_Rigged_APose
cathexis_hot_walk_106_source
cathexis_mirror_48_source
cathexis_sway_415_source
cathexis_head_hold_391_source

Report actual clip name, duration, joint count, root translation and root rotation, whether mesh/skin/textures are embedded, and any visible intersections. Do not certify clearance from catalog previews. Inspect the full costume on this rig. Keep source motion intact; any in-place or clearance-corrected version must be a separately named derivative.

HARD CHARACTER RULES

The existing approved stand-in export is Animation_Confident_Walk_withSkin.fbx; catalog source 106 Confident_Walk is the matching name candidate. Confirm the exact take against our approved reference. Do not silently substitute Confident_Strut, Flirty_Strut, Stage_Walk or another gait.
- She NEVER runs and has NO alert state. Do not bundle run/sprint/alert as gameplay fallbacks. A reaction can interrupt a relaxed pose without creating an alert stance.
- Normal behavior: chilling, vibing, flirting and theatrical social gestures. Coarse work and contamination often provoke frustration. Dirt and mood are related but remain independent.

prompts.title: Signature actions
prompts.text:
CATHEXIS — signature actions to author after the actual body and masks exist

These are custom briefs, NOT verified catalog entries. If your Agent interface cannot generate custom motions, state that and leave them pending. The Meshy Text-to-Motion API is a possible separate experiment; we can also author these offline. Neither route guarantees exact mask contact or costume clearance.

1. POISED IDLE (4–6 seconds, loop)
She settles onto one hip, raises her chin a fraction, slowly checks the audience and makes one small dismissive wrist flourish. Hold still long enough for the pause to feel intentional. Return seamlessly. No ordinary worker fidget or neutral breathing loop.

2. MASK REVEAL (5–7 seconds, one-shot)
She holds eye contact, raises a hand to the temple latch, grips the faceplate, lifts it forward clear of the head and lowers it just beside her shoulder. Hold the exposed mechanism for a beat. Hand contact and the mask's rigid trajectory must be authored against the fitted prop.

3. MASK EXCHANGE (6–9 seconds, staged at a theatre rack)
She lifts the old mask, seats it on a known rack hook, selects another and settles it onto the head rim with a small decisive head tilt. Finish in a different composed pose. Keep both prop positions continuous; no invisible disappearing mask or hand through face.

4. INVITE ONE WORKER (4–6 seconds)
A measured turn toward one person, palm opened low, a teasing beckon, then an expectant hold. The worker may approach or refuse; Cathexis must not clap or celebrate regardless of the response. Exact partner placement is an offline paired scene.

5. DISMISS (3–4 seconds)
She looks the recipient up and down, tips her chin, turns one wrist in a small cutting dismissal and turns away before they finish answering. Precision and a held pause, not frantic waving.

6. HOLD THE ROOM / RALLY (6–8 seconds)
She collects attention with a small raised hand, opens her arms in a measured expansion, singles out an imagined listener and ends on one emphatic cue. Strong silhouette readable from CCTV. Crowd response is separate and driven by the simulation.

7. GRIEF AS PERFORMANCE (5–7 seconds)
A hand suspended near the chest, a long bowed head, a controlled opening toward the audience as if asking them to witness a loss. The mask supplies the face; the body supplies the performance. No guaranteed sincerity encoded in the clip.

8. THE LINE IS BENEATH ME (5–7 seconds)
At a waist-height station she approaches reluctantly, touches the object with exaggerated distaste, recoils and inspects or wipes dirt from her fingers. Provide a continuation that resumes the attempt with obvious resentment, and a separate refusal/appeal ending. This is not automatically a failed task: original conveyor success art still shows her dirty and angry. Exact object contact and task outcome remain our responsibility.

9. LOSING THE AUDIENCE (6–8 seconds)
An invitation receives no response. She repeats it more broadly, freezes when it fails, touches the mask as if checking it and lets the pose collapse. Preserve a readable attempt and recovery before any larger tantrum.

10. OFFENDED EXIT (locomotion with a stationary gesture)
A dismissive turn and look back lead into the approved Hot Walk. She does not run, hurry into another gait, or enter alert. Preserve attitude, heel and skirt clearance; authored starts/stops/turn blends must connect to Hot Walk. If danger prevents a safe walking route, the simulation must handle that situation rather than silently replacing the gait.

11. CONTAMINATED AT THE BREWERY (5–7 seconds)
She withdraws a sticky hand from a known vat-side task, holds it far away from the ivory dress, spreads the fingers and inspects the residue. A sharp recoil becomes an angry glance at a supervisor or worker. Keep a safe grasp/contact phase on the other hand if bracing against the vat. Author hand placement and the partner's position offline. Do not substitute fighting or a happy grin.

12. THE GALLERY IS TOLERABLE (5–7 seconds, loop with contact markers)
She makes a precise adjustment at the loom, rests her head languidly against one hand, checks the result with apparent boredom, and returns to a small exact adjustment. Fine motor skill is visible even when enthusiasm is absent. Match the actual loom handles; no generic hammering or heavy lifting.

13. SECURITY IS NOT MY CONCERN (4–6 seconds, staged exit)
She glances at a form, lets it fall with a dismissive wrist, turns her back on the checkpoint and leaves with an offended theatrical stride. The paper remains a real prop with a defined release point. Worker movement through the unattended post is a separate simulation response.

14. OVERWHELMED AT THE CONVEYOR (4–6 seconds)
The poised stance contracts. Both hands rise to the sides of the crown, shoulders lift and she holds a furious distressed grimace, then tries to regain composure. No smiling, dancing, head impact or damage implied. Keep hand/crown, hair and forearm clearances. A separate angry confrontation can follow if the simulation selects it.

These scenes need a small finger-pose library and costume tracks. No physical prop exchange is accepted solely because the bare skeleton resembles the action. Keep source takes and cleaned derivatives separate. Dirt follows actual exposure and can persist into a composed gesture; emotional recovery does not clean or repair the robot.

prompts.title: Room conditions
prompts.text:
CATHEXIS — dirt appearances on the ACCEPTED shared body

Choose one of the neutral A-pose dirt references before this step. These images define a surface treatment; they are NOT separate characters or alternative anatomy. Face masks are separate items and should not be baked onto the body.

Preserve the exact accepted body mesh, UVs, skeleton, skin weights and sockets. If your tools cannot preserve them, provide texture references for offline work instead of remeshing. A newly generated dirty body cannot be assumed to share the rig or animation files.

Stage condition: worn cracked ivory, antique brass and black mechanics. She is already aged, not glossy factory-new plastic.

Conveyor condition: dense charcoal soot and black-brown machine oil over much of the pale porcelain, cuffs, fingers, bodice and skirt. Darkened matted cable hair. Black-gray stained skirt with sparse pale edges. Use original conveyor art as the benchmark, not a few decorative splashes. The three A-pose options explore dry soot, wet oil and caked mixed grime; the owner will choose or combine them.

Brewery condition: later retexture using wet olive/green-brown process residue on hands, cuffs, bodice and hem. No fluid simulation or extra body geometry needed. Prepare after the conveyor treatment is chosen; do not infer approval from earlier posed concept sketches.

Keep amber eye/canister identity. No new injury, missing pieces, enlarged armor or combat redesign. No baked scenery, lighting or animation pose in textures. Export named material/texture variants; preserve clean source maps. Report any topology/UV changes honestly.

Dirt is not an angry face. The selected face item and body animation supply presentation. She can be dirty and composed, clean and furious. Actual contamination follows exposure events and does not reset when changing rooms. This brief does not add cleaning or repair gameplay.

prompts.title: Delivery order
prompts.text:
CATHEXIS — delivery order and remaining gates
1. Generate the clean body in A-pose, with permanent head/eyes and a separate facial-insert boundary. Inspect silhouette, two separated legs, costume, heels, hands and rear. Source body drawing's mechanical face is a placement guide, not fused immutable geometry.
2. Generate Grace and the distorted mechanical insert separately. Fit head/eyes/insert/shell offline. Then make Fury, Distress and the half-shell. Finish the other porcelain expressions after the interface is sound.
3. Rig the accepted body and run only the four initial tests in 03-rig-tests. Inspect skirt/hair/arm/heel clearance. Meshy may supply rigid hands rather than fingers; report actual bones. No claim of articulated fingers from a five-finger drawing.
4. After approval, audition the 28 priority motions, then useful candidates from the broader 161-entry name/category inventory. These are not 161 validated CATHEXIS clips. Use only Hot Walk for travel; no running or alert fallback. An expressive catalog name is not proof of the intended performance.
5. Select grime treatment A/B/C before material variants. They are comparison inputs, not three new bodies. Keep the same mesh, UVs and rig; brewery residue can be authored after the material direction is chosen. Dirt can accompany anger without forcing it in every scene.
6. Download original full sources privately, plus neutral and animated textured GLB/FBX. Preserve per-clip names/IDs and actual embedded inventories. All Animations may omit later jobs: verify local files, export missing clips separately.

Custom/offline gaps: sticky-finger disgust, protecting the skirt from grime, mask handling, precise conveyor/vat/loom contacts, Hot Walk starts/stops and paired worker responses. Do not substitute arbitrary gestures or claim these are finished by catalog retargeting.

The kit is ready to START staged generation; no CATHEXIS model, actual shared mask fit, facial rig, motion clearance or gameplay integration is certified yet. A/B/C material selection can wait until the clean master is accepted.
